blocks.text: Master Functional & Technical Requirements Specification
EV Service Centre Operations & Quality Management System integration into the Raymond Gray VMMS
Document status | Development specification — not an approved operational SOP
System title | EV Service Centre Operations & Quality Management System
Design rule | Audit first → reuse/enhance existing → additive migration → test → controlled release
1. Executive specification and scope

The Raymond Gray Vehicle Maintenance Management System (VMMS) shall support end-to-end operation, safety, accountability, evidence capture, quality assurance, customer treatment, inventory, cost recovery and performance management for a multi-brand automotive/EV service centre. This is a requirements baseline for upgrading an already-built application—not a replacement system design. The application must preserve current working features, reuse the existing data model, and introduce additions only where an audited gap exists.

System / programme title: EV Service Centre Operations & Quality Management System. Raymond Gray remains the product/system name. Site, trading brand, contracting entity, address, logos, labour rates, tax treatment and payer agreements are configurable; they must not be embedded into workflow logic. The operational library currently consists of draft SOPs/forms; digitisation does not confer formal approval or technician authority.
2. Design principles and non-functional commitments
Single source of truth: customer, VIN, work order, tasks, costing and evidence linked by stable IDs.
Business logic over documents: forms are views/exports of canonical system records, not separate stores of contradictory data.
Five independent process gates: G1 reception, G2 authorised scope, G3 technical completion, G4 quality/technical release, G5 commercial closure.
Segregation: roles coordinate activities; separately assessed and signed privileges determine technical/financial authority.
Explicit payer responsibility: “free to customer” and “free to Service Centre” are never treated as synonyms.
Evidence-first diagnosis and release; preserve unknown/inconclusive findings honestly.
Configurable standards: SOP revision, approved authority, limits, required inspections, rate cards and case classes.
Responsive, accessible and usable workshop experience; minimal duplicate entry, role-specific task queues.
Secure by design: least privilege, encryption in transit/storage where available, auditable events, backup/restore.
Site/model-specific safety rules must come from approved instructions, not invented technical sequences.
3. Target roles and actions
Persona | Core capabilities | Controls
Service Advisor | Booking, intake, communications, estimate and customer consent, commercial handover | Cannot independently certify safety/repair or decide warranty payer outside authority
Workshop Controller / Job Planner | Workload, task allocation, equipment and availability, WIP escalation | Cannot assign beyond staff authorisation
Technician / Trainee | Diagnosis/repairs within privileges, evidence, time and task sign-off | Trainees require documented supervision; no self-release
Technical Lead | Diagnosis review, scope, specialist escalation and competency-supervised decisions | Not automatically financial approver or independent inspector
Quality Inspector | Critical-task independent verification and quality test evidence | Cannot sign own designated independent inspection
Authorised Release Officer | Final technical release according to named authority | Cannot bypass safety/QA holds
Parts & Inventory | Reservations, receipts, issue/return, supplier claims, counts | Purchases subject to delegation and technical compatibility approval
Warranty / Customer Support | Case handling, coverage evidence, payer proposal, complaint SLA | Cannot unilaterally assign customer liability or waive rights
Finance / Billing | Cost ledger, invoices, receipts, dealer recharge, ageing, write-offs | Financial approval requires named thresholds
Compliance / Records / HR | SOP revisions, audits, CAPA, authorisations, records retention | No retrospective privilege alteration
Head of Service Centre | Oversight, escalations, delegations and management reporting | Approval constrained by agreed legal/financial authority
4. End-to-end service lifecycle
Gate | Minimum required evidence | System behaviour
G1 — Intake | VIN, owner, complaint(s), custody, condition/photographs, mileage/SOC, safety triage | Creates one WO and Cxx lines; hold unsafe vehicle
G2 — Diagnose and authorise | Customer diagnostic consent; findings; task scope; quote; technical and commercial approvals | Locks unauthorised work; versioned estimates and approvals
G3 — Execute | Current technician privilege, task instructions, labour, parts, tests and technician declaration | Blocks task completion without required evidence; records deviations

G4 — QA/release | Critical inspection, functional verification, outstanding faults, risk disposition, release signatory | No release if open safety hold, failed inspection or missing independent check
G5 — Commercial closure | Invoice, named payer allocations, payment/recharge or credit terms, handover acknowledgement | No customer handover before G4; retain outstanding receivables properly
State model and exception handling
Work orders and tasks have separate state machines so one held task does not freeze an unrelated task.
A hold has type, severity, owner, reason, source, affected scope, opened/closed timestamps and release evidence.
A superseded approval remains historical; scope changes produce a new version and approvals cannot be silently reused.
Incident response, hazardous battery quarantine and road recovery create linked cases but do not automatically create repair authorisation.
Cancelled, no-show, duplicate and repeat work are retained and distinguishable; deleting history is not standard workflow.
5. Detailed module requirements
M01 — Governance, documents, audits and CAPA
Controlled document object: reference, alias, title, owner, revision, status (draft/review/approved/effective/superseded), effective date, approvers, distribution and review cycle.
Show only current effective SOPs in employee work instructions; drafts accessible to reviewers with conspicuous labels.
Approval/delegation matrix binds person, role, site, privilege, work class, limits, validity and deputy; every decision snapshots the applicable grant.
Internal audit plans/checklists, findings, severity, corrective/preventive actions, root cause, due date, independent effectiveness verification and closure.
Incident/risk log linked to assets, vehicles, employees, work orders; notification/escalation and management review action tracking.
M02 — Customer/vehicle reception and service advisory
Customer/organisation/contact, vehicle VIN and registration, model/variant/powertrain, history, owner changes and communications preferences.
Appointment calendar with capacity, pre-visit parts planning, reminders and arrival/no-show states.
Check-in: complaints in customer wording, vehicle walkaround photos, odometer, SOC/fuel, accessories, pre-existing damage, keys and custody signature.
Customer communications timeline (notifications, estimate, delays, follow-ups) and customer approval artifacts; no invented consent.
Roadside rescue: incident location, dispatch, safety considerations, recovery provider, charges, transfer of custody and arrival verification.
M03 — Diagnosis, estimates and job planning
WO lines for complaint C01… and tasks T01… with links to symptoms, findings, manuals and test records.
Diagnostic capture: DTCs, freeze frame, software versions, conditions, photos, measurements, reproduction attempts, diagnostic certainty and residual risk.
Configurable diagnosis authorisation limit and approval evidence; estimate revision control and granular approval by task and payer.
Task dispatch validates staff competence/privilege, equipment availability and approved work scope.
Unexpected findings initiate variation/hold, customer update, revised cost and authorisation.
M04 — Workshop execution, technical QA and release
Task checklists, start/stop timestamps, work instruction revisions, actual labour, parts and nonconformance events.
Technician declaration records exact actions, tests and outcome; task sign-off is attributable and cannot be overwritten.
Independent inspection assignment for safety-critical tasks; segregation enforced by transaction checks.
Post-repair tests and final scan evidence; status of complaint: resolved, intermittent not reproduced, monitoring, unresolved, unsafe.
Named technical release signature with hard stop on unresolved safety holds; released vehicle locks critical work evidence against silent changes.
M05 — HV safety, battery and emergency readiness
Internal EV/HV authorisation classes, approved vehicle/model privileges, assessed competence, permit validity, supervision and restrictions.
HV task and risk flags trigger gated references to approved model-specific instructions and permits; do not code generic isolation technical values.
Battery impact/thermal/water ingress concerns, quarantine location, escalation, exclusion boundaries and specialist acceptance recorded.
Emergency readiness: shift controllers, verified contacts, evacuation/muster records, drills and incident response evidence.
Unsafe vehicle/asset hold blocks affected job or vehicle release regardless of commercial approvals.
M06 — Parts, procurement and traceability
Catalogue and alternatives with manufacturer part number, variant fitment, approved equivalent and supporting compatibility evidence.
Requisition tied to WO/task or approved stock replenishment; request/technical approval/financial PO approval are separate.
Goods receipt and quarantine records, serial/batch/supplier lot, inspection, stock allocation, issue/return and reserved quantities.
Trace critical fitted part from supplier/PO/receipt to VIN and task, and removed part to custody/disposition/claim.
Reorder levels, ABC/critical spares, backorder visibility, stock counts/variance approvals and supplier nonconformance.
M07 — Warranty, complaints, rework and payer responsibility
Warranty case with sale date, customer representations (written and disputed oral), coverage evidence, sales/dealer obligation and technical causation.
Cost lines with separate proposed and approved payer: customer, dealership, Service Centre, supplier, insurer/logistics, manufacturer, undecided.
Explicit labour/parts/diagnostics/recovery charges and internal recharge; approved goodwill/discount/write-off transactions.
Repeat complaint/rework links original WO, cause, corrective action, cost and responsible budget subject to evidence.
Supplier/insurance recovery independent of initial payer; claim submissions, outcomes, received funds, shortfalls and ageing.
Customer rights and safety controls cannot be overridden by an unresolved internal payer dispute.
M08 — Personnel, training and written authorisations
Employee profiles, grades, qualifications and experience distinct from named task privileges.
Skills matrix for vehicle model/system/tasks, supervised task records, curriculum/trainer attendance, practical assessment evidence.
Written authorisation with assessor, grantor, scope, restrictions, expiry, suspension and reinstatement; history preserved.
At assignment and signoff, verify active privilege and supervision; retrospective privilege changes never rewrite historical authorisation.
Training reminders, expiring certifications and management competency coverage dashboard.
M09 — Equipment, calibration and facility control
Asset register with serial, owner, custodian, commissioning acceptance, location and required inspections.
Calibration certificates, verification, expiry and affected job impact assessment if tool found out of tolerance.
Daily/pre-use inspection for lifts and critical test instruments with serviceable/quarantined status.
Preventive maintenance, fault/quarantine, vendor servicing, tool custody, stocktake and data sanitisation on disposal.
Facility readiness issues/MEP/ventilation/fire/waste punch list with contractor owner and Service Centre technical acceptance recorded separately.
M10 — Finance, operations and management intelligence
Configurable approved rate cards by labour class, service, customer contract, parts markup and currency; tax calculation follows current finance configuration.
Cost by task/WO/case: hours, parts, subcontract, recovery/transport, discounts, write-offs; gross margin and cost-centre allocation.
Invoice/receipt and payer account ledger; dealership warranty recharges, claims, aged debt and recovery reconciliation.
Daily WIP/throughput/holds, staff utilisation, actual vs sold hours, first-time-fix, rework, backlog, turnaround, parts fill rate and safety indicators.
Weekly operations review and monthly manager scorecard with drill-down to source records, definitional metadata and export.
6. Business rules and validation matrix
Rule | System-enforced behaviour
BR-01 | One controlling work order per visit; many complaint, task, evidence and payer lines.
BR-02 | New repair scope requires its own valid authorisation; diagnostic consent is insufficient.
BR-03 | Technical privilege is named, valid, scoped and tested at action time.
BR-04 | Critical QA inspection is independent when the inspection matrix requires it.
BR-05 | Unsafe/HV/incident holds override commercial urgency and block affected release.
BR-06 | Technical release and commercial closure require different evidence and may have different signatories.
BR-07 | Warranty coverage decision and internal payer allocation are separate records.
BR-08 | Zero customer charge requires an alternative approved budget payer or explicit authorised write-off.
BR-09 | Claim recovery cannot be treated as cash received until payment is reconciled.
BR-10 | Inconclusive diagnosis cannot be automatically marked repaired; disposition and residual risk recorded.
BR-11 | Part fitment needs compatible vehicle variant and traceable approval where relevant.
BR-12 | Equipment out of service blocks affected tasks; assess historical work impacted by calibration failures.
BR-13 | Historical records are appended/versioned, never silently rewritten.
BR-14 | No unauthorised individual may approve their own delegated financial exception.
BR-15 | Document approval only by assigned reviewer/approver; a published template is not SOP approval.
BR-16 | Urgent safety safeguarding and billing approvals are logged separately; do not delay protective action to settle payer.
7. Conceptual entity and relationship design

These conceptual domains are implementation-neutral. Map each to existing models where possible. The same vehicle must not be replicated between workshop, warranty and inventory modules. Each object should include tenant/site partition, stable ID, created/updated metadata, lifecycle status and policy-based visibility.
Concept | Key fields | Links
Vehicle | VIN (unique within tenant), brand/model/variant/powertrain, history | Customer, WorkOrder, WarrantyCase
WorkOrder | WO reference, visit/custody, gate/current status, site, opened/closed | Vehicle, Complaints, Tasks, Estimates, Release, Invoice
Complaint/Task | Cxx/Txx, problem/repair scope, diagnostic source, owner, state | WO, Evidence, PartsIssue, Labour, Approval
Approval/Authority | grant ID, action class, actor, scope, threshold, revision, signed evidence | Person, estimate/task/finance or QA event
SafetyHold/Permit | type/severity, scope, restrictions, resolver, evidence | WO, Vehicle, Asset, Incident
MaterialTransaction | SKU, lot/serial, quantity, custody, cost, disposition | PO, Receipt, Stock, WO/Task, Return
Warranty/PayerLedger | case, coverage, proposed/approved payer, cost line, claim, settlement | WO, Invoice, SupplierClaim, DealerAccount
Inspection/Release | inspection criteria, inspector, results, release actor, time, residual faults | WO, Task, Hold, Test
CompetencyGrant | person, privileges, systems/models, validity, assessor, restrictions | Assignment, Signoff, Training
Document/Quality | doc ref/version/effective state, audit, CAPA, acknowledgement | Task instructions, Evidence, Incident
8. Authority and approval mechanics
Delegation configuration
Separate technical, inspection, release, customer/estimate, finance, governance and emergency privilege classes.
Store named individuals and substitutes, site scope, vehicle classes, signed effective interval, monetary thresholds and conflict-of-interest rules.
A person may hold several functions if allowed, but the mandatory independent inspection check cannot be waived by role overlap.
Every approved action stores a snapshot of authority at that time; access changes or revocation affect future acts.
Unapproved rates/limits remain inactive configuration values requiring management action; the system must not guess thresholds.
9. Detailed reporting and measurement dictionary
Metric | Definition | Breakdown / caveat
Vehicle throughput | Count of distinct WOs G5-closed in period | Day/week/month; segment by payer, make and service class
Work in progress | Open WO by state/hold and ageing | Realtime and daily cutoff
Turnaround time | G5 handover timestamp minus G1 reception | Median, 90th percentile; segment parts/customer holds
Technician utilisation | Recorded productive task time / available scheduled time | Exclude authorised absence; report separately from efficiency
Labour efficiency | Approved/sold standard hours / actual clocked task hours | Only when standard hours available
First-time fix | Eligible completed WOs without linked same-fault return in defined window | Configurable window, exclude unrelated visits
Rework cost | Approved labour+parts+outsourced rework direct cost | By technical cause and approved payer
Dealer warranty receivables | Posted dealer recharges less receipts/credits | Age buckets; unapplied collections separate
Parts fill rate | Task parts fulfilled when required / task parts demand lines | Do not conceal backorder
Diagnostic quality | Complaint lines with evidence and disposition / applicable lines | Exclude N/A documented
Release compliance | Released WOs with all required approvals/checks / released WOs | Goal is 100%, drill down to any exception
HV authorisation coverage | Active named staff privileges vs required task demand | By model/system/site
Customer complaints | Open cases, first response timeliness, resolution and repeat complaints | Avoid implied legal SLA; configurable
Stock variance | Counted minus book quantity/value | By inventory category and approval
10. Screens and user journeys
Screen / workbench | Required decisions and queues
Advisor daily board | Appointments; arriving vehicles; estimate approvals; customer updates; releases pending handover.
Technician task view | Assigned jobs, approved procedure, pre-task safety/privilege, diagnostic capture, parts issue, actual time, sign-off.
Technical lead console | Unresolved diagnostics, risky variations, review queues, qualified dispatch and root-cause investigations.
QA & release desk | Critical inspections pending, failed tests, open holds, required independent signoffs and vehicle release decision.
Parts counter | Reservations/backorders, fitment check, issue/returns, goods receipt, quarantine and supplier claims.
Warranty & payer desk | Case register, claim evidence, payer per cost line, dealer recharges, disputed cases and recoveries.
Compliance view | Effective SOPs, revisions, staff acknowledgements, expiring authorisations, audits/CAPA and incidents.
Manager dashboard | WIP, bottlenecks, safety, revenue/margin, debt, throughput, repeat faults, staff/equipment readiness.
11. Security, integrity and operating reliability
Use the existing authentication strategy; add fine-grained authorization checks in backend services and DB access paths.
Protect sensitive customer information, employee competency records, incident data and photos through least-privilege roles and site segregation.
Audit significant read/export actions where sensitive data is involved; record every modification to safety, approval and finance records.
Sensitive evidence must use controlled storage with document hashes where feasible, limited signed access and backup coverage.
Encrypt in transit and at rest as supported, use secure session lifecycle, validation, rate limiting and safe logging with secrets redacted.
Write transactions atomically for stock issue, approved cost allocation, release, invoice and payment; use optimistic locking or equivalent concurrency control.
Establish retention schedules by record class and legal requirements via management configuration; allow legal hold and controlled export.
Backups, restore exercises, test/staging environment, disaster recovery and incident monitoring must be part of acceptance.
Provide accessibility, localization for Ghana cedi and other currencies, correct timezone handling and reliable printable outputs.
12. Integrations, data imports and documentation mapping
Preserve existing payment, invoice, reminder, email/WhatsApp, document storage, diagnostic file import and finance interfaces if present.
Where manufacturer-specific diagnostic data cannot be integrated automatically, allow traceable upload and manual indexed metadata without pretending to have direct vehicle access.
Allow vehicle history and existing invoice/report exports while retaining source IDs and revision metadata.

Map SOPs to business workflow validations: SOP 001 intake, 002 technical execution, 003 WO, 004 parts, 005 HV, 006 emergency, 007 warranty/payer, 008 competency, 009 equipment, 010 finance, GOV 001–004 governance.
Preserve legacy reference codes and document aliases; canonical naming to be approved before operational Issue 1.0.
Do not convert the 105 master-register entries automatically into 105 separate software modules; group into workflows, reports, templates and controlled records.
13. Migration and delivery roadmap
Phase | Scope | Exit evidence
0 — Discover | Repository/DB/workflow audit and requirement mapping; no destructive changes. | Audit, gap map and change-control decision
1 — Core controls | WO IDs, complaint/task model, approvals, holds and G1–G5 events; reuse existing job card. | Traceable end-to-end pilot
2 — Safety and QA | Privilege check, critical inspections, model-specific permit references and release controls. | Safety/QA UAT, named authority setup
3 — Commercial recovery | Payer ledger, warranty, rework, parts and invoicing reconciliation. | Dealer warranty end-to-end financial pilot
4 — Asset and governance | Equipment readiness, training, document control, audit/CAPA and emergency records. | Operational readiness evidence
5 — Reporting/launch | Dashboards, staff guides, regression, production pilot, 30-day audit. | Signed management acceptance and staged issue
14. Detailed acceptance scenarios
AT-01 — Existing vehicle/service records and invoices remain accessible; no duplicates/ID changes.
AT-02 — Second customer complaint creates C02 on same WO, independently diagnosable.
AT-03 — Technician cannot perform HV-restricted task without current model/task privilege and permit.
AT-04 — Diagnostic authorisation alone cannot authorise a replacement part.
AT-05 — Extra cost over approval threshold holds only affected task; revised approval resumes.
AT-06 — A technician cannot perform a required independent check on their own critical task.
AT-07 — Unresolved intermittent fault routes to disposition and release risk decision.
AT-08 — Technical release cannot occur with open safety hold, failed test or missing evidence.
AT-09 — No commercial handover without technical release.
AT-10 — Free-to-customer dealer warranty work posts dealer payer/recharge with receivable tracking.
AT-11 — Supplier recovery is tracked independently from immediate internal payer.
AT-12 — Rework links original WO and cause, with authorised payer and measured repeat rate.
AT-13 — Part issued by lot/serial for compatible VIN; wrong-variant part blocked/quarantined.
AT-14 — Expired calibration / failed lift pre-use check blocks equipment-dependent task.
AT-15 — Expired/revoked authority blocks future approval but preserves historical proof.
AT-16 — Audit trail records immutable previous/new state, actor, timestamps, reason.
AT-17 — Legacy statuses, invoice reports and integrations pass regression tests.
AT-18 — Race condition: two users cannot release same WO with conflicting holds.
AT-19 — Permission/tenant leakage tests prevent cross-site and unauthorised record access.
AT-20 — Backups, restore, deployment and rollback/recovery are exercised.
15. Approval dependencies, assumptions and exclusions
Management configuration pending
Written named technical/QA/release privilege schedule, roles and substitutes.
Financial delegations, rate cards, goodwill authority, internal dealer recharge terms, account codes and payment terms.
Effective controlled SOP revisions, retention schedules, legal entity name and privacy notices.
Site-specific EV/HV emergency, inspection, equipment commissioning and model-specific technical validation.
Approval that testing supports Issue 1.0—draft technical documents alone do not authorise operational deployment.
Excluded assumptions
No assumption about programming language, hosting provider, database engine or device platform.
No forced replacement of current screens, customer/invoice identifiers or accounting systems.
No manufacturer warranty coverage presumed for imported vehicles and no legal allocation of customer liability without evidence.
No procedural instructions for actual HV isolation derived from generic software rules.
No automatic issuance of staff privileges or financial approval limits from job titles.
No software go-live presented as operational or regulatory certification.
16. Developer traceability and issue-control deliverables

For each requirement create a trace line: requirement ID → referenced SOP/record → existing feature and code/table → gap classification → planned implementation → migration → server-side control → UAT case → evidence → owner/decision → completion status. Output an as-built system map, updated data dictionary, admin configuration matrix and user manuals.

Recommendation: the implementation prompt is issued to the software development agent with this master specification and the full controlled draft documentation library as attachments. Confirm requirements against the actual installed application; enhancements must be additive and justified. Final Issue 1.0 approval remains a management decision based on completed validation evidence.
